howDoI.q: How do I make scenery that slides past forever?
How do I make near things slide faster than far ones?
How do I make a monster go round and round?
How do I turn a monster's picture as it goes?
How do I keep a door shut until something happens?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Round and Round is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a few minutes to finish. It is in the Showcase Tricks group, because it shows how a big game goes round: a road that slides past, and a car that drives a loop. It is the follow-on to To the Horizon, which drove into the distance.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door to go on.

Each level is one screen that never scrolls. Nothing in this game hurts you.

pages.head: Level 1: The Road Goes By
pages.html:
Level 1: The Road Goes By

Mia stands on the bed of a truck. The THE LAST BLOCK TURNS BACK INTO THE FIRST sign stands on the left, and the NEAR THINGS SLIDE FASTER sign stands to its right. Behind her, blue hills, a row of trees and a stone rail slide past, one after another, as if the truck were driving along. The hills are slow, the trees faster and the rail fastest.

The truck is not going anywhere. The scenery is a few strips of blocks that change their pictures, and the door in the back of the cab is open from the start. Stay a while and watch the strips first.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • A ring of blocks. Open bw1.bbl and look at the blocks for the hills. Each one is the same strip of hills seen through a window that has slid 4 pixels along, and each has a Next block (the one after it) and a Time of 14 ticks. The last block of the ring has the first as its Next block, so the strip slides and starts over, forever. There are 10 blocks in the hills' ring, 16 in the trees' (two rows of 8) and 4 in the rail's. Every strip is painted to repeat every 40 pixels, so its ring comes back to where it began.
  • Near is faster. The hills move 4 pixels every 14 ticks, the trees 5 pixels every 2 ticks and the rail 10 pixels every 2 ticks. There are 18.2 ticks in a second. Slower for far and faster for near is what makes a flat picture look deep.
  • Neighbors start apart. A strip is 40 pixels wide and a block 20, so the blocks along a row come in two kinds, the ring's block and the one half a ring away. Open one.map and see that the blocks alternate along each row. They turn on the same clock, so they slide together and the strip stays seamless.
  • The truck is still. The deck, the tail board and the cab are ordinary solid blocks, and the door is two plain blocks with a link. Mia walks on the deck; only the pictures behind her change. The scene never scrolls: in bw.gam its four scrolling settings are off.
  • Budget. The level uses 120 of the 150 blocks it may have. A ring costs one block for every window of its picture, so a smoother slide, with a smaller step, costs more blocks.
  • The signs. Each sign is a few ordinary blocks side by side, with the words drawn in their pictures.

pages.head: Level 2: Round the Loop
pages.html:
Level 2: Round the Loop

A round track hangs in the sky and a little orange car drives round it, nose up the right side, upside down across the top and nose down the left. In the middle three lamps are dark. The END WHERE YOU START AND IT LOOPS sign stands on the left, and the LAMPS COUNT THE LAPS sign stands on the right.

Each time the car gets home to the checkered line at the bottom, a lamp lights. When the third is lit, about 18 seconds after the level begins, the bars on the door lift. Walk up to it and wait. The car cannot hurt you.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • A path that ends where it began. Open bw.mon and pick the car. Its path is eight corners, each a few blocks right or left and up or down from where the car started, and the last corner is the place it started from. After a corner with no speed, or after the tenth corner, a monster that never dies starts its path again from where it stands, so the car goes round forever. A path holds at most 10 corners.
  • Straight pieces. A path is straight lines between its corners, so the loop is eight pieces, an octagon, and the car's blocks follow it. The track under it is a painted circle, wide enough that the car stays on the road at the corners.
  • The picture turns. Each corner also has an orientation: how the picture is drawn while the monster walks to that corner. There are eight, the picture turned a quarter at a time or turned over. The car is drawn once, facing right, with its wheels down. On the right side it is turned nose up, across the top upside down, down the left side nose down, so its wheels always face the track.
  • Speed. Every corner also has a speed in pixels a tick. The car's is 3, so a lap takes 112 ticks, a little over 6 seconds. Its two pictures, with the wheel's hub in different places, change every 3 ticks.
  • Lamps on the clock. A block cannot see the car, so the lamps count by time. Each lamp in bw2.bbl has a Next block that is the lit lamp and a Time of 112, 224 or 336 ticks from the level's start. If the car were faster or slower, the lamps would have to change with it.
  • The barred door. The door is two blocks, each solid with red and white bars over it, that turn into the plain door after 336 ticks. A solid block stops Mia; the plain door has a link, so the door works when the bars lift.
  • Its own block file. This level's blocks are in bw2.bbl, 100 of the 150 that a block set may hold. The hedges at both sides close the room in.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

This is a picture of going round, not a world that goes round:

  • Nothing moves but pictures. The truck does not drive; each strip is a ring of blocks changing pictures. And a ring only slides as fast as its steps: a smaller step is smoother but costs more blocks, out of 150.
  • A strip's blocks all change together, on a clock that starts when the level starts. The scenery cannot speed up when Mia presses a key or slow down when she stops.
  • A path is at most 10 corners of straight lines, so a circle is an octagon, or a few more sides. The engine cannot curve a path.
  • A picture turns only a quarter at a time, or turns over. On a slanted piece the car keeps the nearest of its four facings, so its nose is a little off. It is turned by corner, not by frame.
  • Blocks cannot see monsters, and a monster cannot count laps. The lamps and the door run on time, and they keep the same time even if the car were stopped.
  • A monster's path is the same every time. It cannot decide to go round faster on a later lap.
  • A block set holds at most 150 blocks, and the rings, the signs and the big painting share them.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In bw1.bbl change the Time of the trees' blocks from 2 to 4 and see them slow down.
  • In bw.mon raise the car's speed from 3 to 6 and watch the lamps fall behind. Then change the lamps' Time in bw2.bbl to match.
  • Give the car one more corner, if you can make it fit in 10.
  • Draw the car in a different color, or a different vehicle, in bw.mbl.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
